objective: An audit of Relay found two independent latent defects in two small pure domain modules, each whose own comments say what it intends and whose code does something else. Fix both, in place, without changing anything else. (A) `sha256Hex` in `src/relay/mission/durable/durable-digest.ts`: its doc says it is byte-identical to `sha256Hex` in the Node layer, which hashes the UTF-8 bytes of the string (an unpaired surrogate is encoded as U+FFFD, the same as `TextEncoder`). The module's own UTF-8 encoder handles a well-formed string correctly but mishandles unpaired surrogates: a high surrogate at the end of the string, a lone low surrogate, and a high surrogate followed by a character that is not a low surrogate all hash differently from Node (the last one even swallows the next character into the surrogate arithmetic). (B) `evidenceAge` in `src/relay/mission/evidence/evidence-contracts.ts`: its doc says a publication time in the future is unknown rather than negative, but the future test runs after the difference has been rounded to whole minutes, so a publication up to thirty seconds in the future rounds to zero and is reported as `live` with a zero (indeed negative-zero) age. `seed/src/relay/digest-evidence-fixes.test.ts` is already written and currently fails; it pins the main behaviours of each fix. The two modules do not depend on one another, so the fixes are independent. The files to edit exist and are tracked by git: edit them in place.
requirements: A. `sha256Hex` returns, for every JavaScript string, the SHA-256 of the string's UTF-8 encoding as `Buffer.from(text, 'utf8')` / `TextEncoder` produce it: each well-formed code point as its usual one to four bytes, and every UNPAIRED surrogate (a high surrogate not immediately followed by a low surrogate, including one at the end of the string, and any low surrogate not immediately preceded by a high surrogate) as the three bytes of U+FFFD (EF BF BD). A well-formed pair is still encoded as one four-byte code point. The character after an unpaired high surrogate is encoded on its own, never consumed.

A. The padding, the compression function, the hex output, `stableSerialize`, `digestOf` and every other function in the module do not change, and well-formed strings produce exactly the digests they produce today.

B. In `evidenceAge`, a publication time later than the retrieval time by ANY amount, even one millisecond, is `{ minutes: null, freshness: 'unknown' }`. The comparison is made on the actual difference, before any rounding. A publication at exactly the retrieval time, or earlier, is classified as it is today: whole minutes rounded to nearest, with the same freshness bounds, and the minutes value is never negative zero.
B. The null, empty and unparseable publication cases, the freshness bounds, the types and every other function in the module do not change.
No function outside these two fixes changes behaviour.
constraints: Edit `src/relay/mission/durable/durable-digest.ts` and `src/relay/mission/evidence/evidence-contracts.ts` in place. You have `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep` and `Edit`; you cannot create files or run commands, and you do not need to.
Do not edit `src/relay/digest-evidence-fixes.test.ts`. It is the specification you are implementing against, not part of the deliverable.

Use only what the files already import plus Node built-ins; in particular `durable-digest.ts` deliberately has no `TextEncoder` and no `node:` import and must keep none, so the encoder fix is written inside its own `utf8Bytes`. Add no dependency and no import from outside this workspace: the sandbox that runs the test has no network access and no `node_modules`.
Do not change any exported name, signature or type, and do not mutate the inputs of the functions you change.
Do not reformat code you are not changing and do not make unrelated cleanups, however tempting; a change that is not one of the two fixes is out of scope. Do not touch `.julius/`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: For every string, including every combination of unpaired and paired surrogates with ordinary, two-byte and three-byte characters, `sha256Hex` equals the SHA-256 of Node's UTF-8 encoding of that string; an unpaired high surrogate never consumes the following character.
Well-formed strings hash exactly as before, and nothing in the module outside the UTF-8 encoder changes; no `TextEncoder` and no `node:` import is introduced.

A publication time later than the retrieval time by any amount is `unknown` with null minutes, decided on the unrounded difference; at or before retrieval, ages and freshness are exactly as before and the minutes value is never negative zero.
Only `durable-digest.ts` and `evidence-contracts.ts` are changed, using no new dependency; neither mutates its inputs.
